title: Static and dynamic 3D culture of neural precursor cells on macroporous cryogel microcarriers
author: Newland, Ehret, et al.
materials: The cryogel microcarriers were prepared in a manner similar to that reported previously [1]. For preparation of the hydrogel precursor solution a molar ratio of four-arm amino-terminated PEG (10 kDa, JenKem Technology USA) to heparin (14 kDa, Sodium Salt, Porcine Intestinal Mucosa, Calbiochem, Merck) of 1:1 was used. A molar ratio of 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide (EDC, Sigma-Aldrich) to N-hydroxysulfosuccinimide sodium salt (sulfo-NHS, Sigma) of 2:1 was used. 1 % of the heparin used in the cryogel microcarrier preparation was Alexa 647 labelled (prepared from Alexa 647, Invitrogen as reported previously [1]). All components were dissolved in deionized, decarbonized water (MilliQ) by vortexing and ultrasonication and were kept on ice afterwards. Activation of carboxylic acid groups of heparin was performed by mixing the EDC, sulfo-NHS and heparin solutions and leaving them on ice for 15 min. Then the PEG solution was added and 600 μL of this final precursor solution were immediately injected into a mixture of 9 mL toluene and 3 mL of a Synperonic PEP105 (Sigma-Aldrich) in toluene solution (c =1 mg/mL, as a stabilizing agent). The resulting emulsion was stirred at 700 rpm for 10 min at room temperature for droplet formation to occur, before another 3 mL of Synperonic PEP105 in toluene solution (1 mg/mL) were added to the stirring solution to avoid droplet agglomeration. Subsequently, the flask containing the emulsion was immersed into a −80 °C ethanol bath for 2 h. The resulting microcarriers were kept at −20 °C over-night and subsequently lyophilized for at least 24 h, before they were dispersed in ethanol and afterwards washed several times with MilliQ water.

To determine the percentage of dead cells, a live-dead solution calcein AM Solution (PromoKine) and propidium iodide (Sigma) was added to cells cultured on microcarriers in NB + B27 medium and incubated for 20 min at 37 °C. Cells were counterstained with Hoechst 33342 1:1000 in DPBS for 10 min and washed with NB medium once. For the cell harvesting experiment, microcarriers with cells were pelleted at 50 g for 1 min, followed by incubation in 500 μl accumax or accutase for 5 min. The cells were washed once in PBS, and then resuspended in PBS containing trypan blue and analyzed using a Countess 2 cell counter (Life Technologies). The number and percentage of viable cells was counted. The microcarriers were then analyzed separately by qualitative confocal microscopy.

steps.title: Prepare hydrogel precursor solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve four‑arm amino‑terminated PEG (10 kDa, JenKem) and heparin (14 kDa, Calbiochem) at a 1:1 molar ratio, together with EDC and sulfo‑NHS at a 2:1 molar ratio, in deionized, decarbonized MilliQ water; vortex and ultrasonicate, keep the solution on ice, and include 1 % Alexa‑647‑labelled heparin.

steps.title: Activate heparin carboxyl groups
steps.instruction: Mix the EDC, sulfo‑NHS and heparin solutions and incubate on ice for 15 min, then add the PEG solution.

steps.title: Form emulsion and freeze‑dry microcarriers
steps.instruction: Inject 600 µL of the final precursor solution into 9 mL toluene containing 3 mL Synperonic PEP105 (1 mg/mL) in toluene; stir at 700 rpm for 10 min at room temperature, add an additional 3 mL Synperonic PEP105 (1 mg/mL) to prevent droplet agglomeration, then immerse the flask in a –80 °C ethanol bath for 2 h. Keep the resulting microcarriers at –20 °C overnight, lyophilize for ≥24 h, disperse in ethanol and wash several times with MilliQ water.

steps.title: Functionalize microcarriers with RGD peptide
steps.instruction: For RGD functionalisation, place 5 mg dry microcarriers in 1.5 mL phosphate buffer (pH 5) containing sterile‑filtered EDC (28.8 mg) and sulfo‑NHS (16.3 mg) (2:1 molar ratio) and shake at 400 rpm for 45 min at 4 °C. Exchange the buffer to borate buffer (pH 8) and add cyclic peptide cyclo(Arg‑Gly‑Asp‑D‑Tyr‑Lys) at 200 µg/mL (dissolved in the same borate buffer); incubate 2 h at room temperature while shaking at 400 rpm. Wash the functionalised microcarriers three times with MilliQ water, freeze in liquid nitrogen and lyophilize.

steps.title: Immunocytochemistry staining
steps.instruction: Fix 2D NPC cultures and cells on microcarriers with 4 % PFA in PBS, permeabilise with 0.1 % Triton‑X100 for 15 min, block with 10 % donkey serum for 30 min, then incubate overnight at 4 °C in blocking solution with the chosen primary antibody pair (rabbit anti‑Sox2 1:400 + mouse anti‑nestin 1:250; or rabbit anti‑PCNA 1:1000 + mouse anti‑nestin 1:250; or rabbit anti‑GFAP 1:250 + mouse anti‑Map2 1:1000). Wash three times with 1X DPBS, incubate 3 h at room temperature in the dark with donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and donkey anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) secondary antibodies in blocking solution, wash again with 1X DPBS, counterstain with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 in DPBS) for 10 min, and perform a final DPBS wash.

steps.title: Live‑dead staining and cell harvesting
steps.instruction: Add calcein‑AM solution (PromoKine) and propidium iodide (Sigma) to cells on microcarriers cultured in NB + B27 medium and incubate 20 min at 37 °C; counterstain with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 in DPBS) for 10 min and wash once with NB medium. For harvesting, pellet microcarriers at 50 g for 1 min, incubate in 500 µL Accumax or Accutase for 5 min, wash once in PBS, resuspend in PBS containing trypan blue, and count viable cells with a Countess 2 cell counter. Keep the microcarriers for separate confocal microscopy.

steps.title: Confocal microscopy imaging
steps.instruction: Immediately after live‑dead staining, image cells on a Dragonfly spinning‑disc confocal microscope at 20× magnification. For quantitative analysis acquire 15 z‑stacks per condition covering 40 µm depth with 1 µm step size. For qualitative images acquire 40 µm and 80 µm z‑stacks with 0.5 µm steps. Capture a single cross‑section image of each microcarrier to determine its diameter.

steps.title: Image processing and analysis
steps.instruction: Process images in ImageJ: subtract background with a rolling‑ball radius of 5 pixels, count nuclei automatically with 3D Objects Counter v2.0 (size filter ≥100), obtain mean totals for all cells, dead cells, Sox2‑positive and PCNA‑positive cells; count Map2‑ and GFAP‑positive cells manually, calculate ratios of each marker to total cells and plot. Process qualitative images with Imaris software.

description: Microcarriers were characterized in terms of size and pore size and live dead analysis of neural precursor cells cultured on the microcarriers was carried out in proliferative and differentiation conditions [5]. Live cells (green) can be seen adhered to the microcarrier (red) with nuclear counterstaining (blue) and few dead cells (orange). Such analysis can be used to validate the growth of the cells within the pores of the microcarriers. Scale bars represent 100 μm.
